newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Timorese in asylum bid at Jakarta's French mission.
newsitem.headline: Timorese in asylum bid at Jakarta's French mission.

text.p: Four East Timorese men broke into the French embassy in Jakarta before dawn on Tuesday to seek political asylum, witnesses said.

They said the four scaled the three-metre (nine-foot) high spiked iron fence surrounding the French embassy compound in central Jakarta, unfurling a banner while shouting "Viva East Timor" and other pro-independence slogans.
"We are seeking political asylum in France," one of the four men said through the fence soon after entering the compound.
"We are being chased by the Indonesian armed forces for taking part in a demonstration in (the East Timor capital) Dili in November," another asylum seeker said.
The demonstration took place on November 25 outside the offices of Nobel laureate Bishop Carlos Belo after he gave a news conference attended by local and foreign media.
A French diplomat confirmed there were East Timorese in the embassy but declined to provide any further details.
An official from the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) said they had been informed by the French embassy that there were four Timorese men in the mission.
East Timorese sources identified the men as Ru Ximenes, 26, Akilis Siqueira, 21, Bonifacio Cardoso Diaz, 18, and Siquito Valenti, 18, all from Los Palos on the eastern tip of the territory.

The break-in came before talks between the seven-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and the European Union (EU) in Singapore next week where East Timor has been raised a possible sticking point.
Two of the four men said they were high school students while the other two said they were students at the University of East Timor in Dili.

The men were met by two embassy officials in plain clothes and body searched before being taken inside a building within the compound. One Indonesian soldier and a policeman watched from outside the compound fence.

Since September 1995, 96 young East Timorese who have broken into foreign embassies in Jakarta have been given asylum in Portugal, the former colonial power in the enclave invaded by Indonesia in December 1975.
The United Nations does not recognise Indonesia's 1976 annexation of East Timor and regards Portugal as the administering power in the territory.
The men said they did not want asylum in Portugal.
"There are already many of our brothers in Portugal. We want to go to France," one of the men said.
It is has been the Indonesian government's policy to allow such asylum seekers to leave unhindered with their travel to Portugal facilitated by the ICRC.
